title: Pulmonary acinus: alveoli and gas-exchange barrier
description: From terminal bronchiole to alveolar sac, type I/II pneumocytes, macrophages and the air–blood barrier.

questions.question: What is a pulmonary acinus?
questions.answer: It is the region distal to a terminal bronchiole containing respiratory bronchioles, alveolar ducts and alveoli where gas exchange occurs.

questions.question: What is the air-blood barrier in an alveolus?
questions.answer: The exchange surface includes alveolar epithelium, thin shared basement-membrane regions and capillary endothelium, allowing short diffusion distances.

questions.question: What is the terminal bronchiole?
questions.answer: Final nonalveolated conducting airway before respiratory zone. Function: Delivers air to downstream acinus.

questions.question: Where is the alveolar duct located?
questions.answer: Distal passage whose walls are largely alveolar openings. Function: Distributes air to multiple alveolar sacs.

questions.question: What is the function of the alveolus?
questions.answer: Function: Provides extensive diffusion surface. Tiny airspace lined by specialized epithelium and surrounded by capillaries.
